key_insight: Particle trapping in a time-periodic vortex fails abruptly when outward inertia-driven drift overcomes inward thermophoretic migration, triggering a saddle-node bifurcation.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a tunable threshold for predicting when heated-flow systems can retain or release inertial particles, useful for particle separation and thermal transport design.
method: Derived a small-Stokes-number, cycle-averaged radial migration model for slow particle motion.
Analyzed fixed points of the reduced dynamics to locate trapping states and separatrices.
Used phase portraits, bifurcation diagrams, and asymptotic analysis to show trapping-loss via saddle-node bifurcation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical validation through reduced-model analysis and additional calculations across multiple velocity and temperature profiles, showing the mechanism is robust.
watch_item: The result relies on asymptotic reduction in the small-Stokes-number regime, so accuracy may degrade for larger inertia or strongly nonperiodic flows.
paper_title: Trapping-loss transition via a saddle-node bifurcation in thermophoretic particle transport driven by a time-periodic vortex
